Hi Tom / Lisa,

Great to meet you both on the call this morning — thanks for walking through your ingestion patterns and retention requirements. As promised, a quick recap of next steps and answers to the data residency/region-pinning questions we discussed: 

1) Region pinning behavior
- You can pin customer traffic to a specific region (e.g., us-east-1 or eu-west-1) at the account or route level.
- Pinning ensures inference requests and transient state (KV cache) are processed in the pinned region.
- For cross-region failover, we support automated failover to a configured secondary region. Failover keeps serving availability while honoring your policy-level constraints (see failover notes below).

2) PII / logging controls
- We support request-level redaction rules and can disable request/response logging for routes that handle PII.
- Audit logs are available for admin actions; application-level payload logs can be routed to your own logging endpoint or disabled.

3) Backups and snapshots
- Model artifacts and configuration metadata are stored in the control plane; backups are encrypted at rest and can be configured to remain in-region.
- Customer-configured backups for stateful artifacts (if you use our optional managed KV store) can be scheduled and are encrypted with your KMS key if you bring one.

Attachments included: Redwood SOC 2 summary (PDF), region pinning architecture diagram (PNG), proposed data retention table (XLSX).

Next steps (proposed):
- Aditya to share a short note on failover semantics + encryption details (cc'd).
- I will send an updated MAP (mutual action plan) with estimated lead times and procurement milestones by EOD tomorrow.
- Please confirm if you require backups to be restricted to a single region or if cross-region replication is acceptable for disaster recovery.

If anything above needs correction, let me know. Happy to jump on another call with your security/infra team.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Hi Tom / Lisa — Aditya here (Solutions Engineering). Quick answers to the technical points — happy to hop on a call if you prefer a walkthrough.

1) Cross-region failover and data residency
- Transient request payloads (inference inputs/responses) are processed in the active region and not persisted to any other region by default.
- During automated failover we have two behaviors depending on your policy: 
  a) Strict residency mode: the system will fail the request rather than route to a region outside the allowed set. No data leaves the pinned region.
  b) DR failover mode: route to secondary region to preserve availability. In this case transient payloads are processed in the secondary region only for the duration of the failover window; we do not persist payloads to long-term storage unless you opt in.

2) Backups / snapshots / replication
- Backups of control-plane metadata and optional managed KV snapshots are configurable: you can restrict backups to a single region or enable cross-region replication for DR.
- By default we do NOT replicate application payload logs or cached KV payloads cross-region unless replication is enabled.
- When cross-region replication is enabled, you can choose to use Redwood-managed encryption keys or bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via your KMS; BYOK ensures only your key can decrypt replicated backups.

3) Encryption & PII handling
- All at-rest storage is encrypted (AES-256). For extra control, we support customer-managed KMS keys for encryption of backups and long-term artifacts.
- Audit logs and admin logs never contain full customer payloads; we can also scrub or truncate logs for routes that handle PII.

4) RTO / RPO expectations
- Automated cross-region failover: targeted RTO ~ 1-3 minutes for routing continuity (depends on DNS/edge caching and your chosen routing policy).
- RPO for optional managed KV store snapshots: configurable, typical options are 5m / 1h / 24h. Restores from snapshots depend on size; typical restore for a 100GB KV is ~30-90 minutes.

If you need formal SLAs or contract language we can include specific commitments in the Dedicated/Private offering. Attaching the region-pinning architecture diagram and the data retention table we discussed.

Regards,
